newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up in late pre-weekend spurt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up in late pre-weekend spurt.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose Friday in a slow, cautious session.
The leading IPC share index ended up 30.32 points, or 0.81 percent, at 3,775.71. Trading volume was dull at 66.5 million shares.
"They wanted to end the week on positive turf, so they took advantage of the lack of sellers," a floor trader said.
Analysts said the investors were awaiting several developments on the economic and political fronts.

"There are several factors on the international front that are keeping the market on hold. The most important is the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25, and then there is the U.S. Senate vote next week," a Mexico City equity analyst said, who requested anonymity.

The Federal Reserve's policy-making FOMC will decide whether to raise U.S. interest rates, while the U.S. Senate is expected to vote on a bill to decertify Mexico as a drug-war ally, perhaps next week.
"Then there are municipal elections this weekend in the state of Morelos this weekend. We believe everything is calm, but it does cause some concern among investors," the analyst added.
On the broad market, a total of 104 stocks changed hands of which 44 ended up while 34 declined.
Traders said gains by airline holding company Cintra and soft-drinks bottler Emvasa helped the overall market.
Cintra ended up 50 centavos (six cents) at 6.90 pesos (87 cents) while Emvasa gained 30 centavos (four cents) to 4.30 pesos (54 cents).
Situr, tourist arm of the Sidek group, was another prominent gainer, up two centavos (less than one cent) to 28 centavos (four cents) on speculative buying, traders said.
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the prominent decliners' list, off six centavos (one cent) to 44 centavos (six cents).
The market fell 1.79 percent on the week and traders expected share prices to see-saw over the coming days.
"Public holidays will make people swifty acquire or dump positions at the start of next week," another dealer added.
